limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local efficacy validation.
Original typed source inventory is not normalized; retain source identities and limits in the procedure/readsets.

applicability.scope: Source-supported diagnosis of training-visible PyTorch DCP save pauses, snapshot/staging/upload lifetimes and bounded CPU staging-buffer reuse; distributed recovery validity and backend durability need separate evidence.
applicability.prerequisites: Known correspondence between the installed PyTorch API and source/version notes, identified checkpointed-state mutation boundaries and an initial one-outstanding-save policy before overlap is considered.
applicability.input_contract: Installed PyTorch revision, stager, storage writer and thread/process executor, checkpoint contents, ranks per host and state-mutation boundaries; performance assessment needs caller/staging/upload waits and host/resource observations.
applicability.produced_artifact: A completion/lifetime diagnosis and smallest justified staging/cache/backpressure lever, with separate caller-pause, staging, upload and step-time measurements proposed for authorized validation.
applicability.failure_modes: Mutating source state before staging completes, overwriting cached snapshots before prior upload completes, ignoring caller-side state_dict work or treating async return as durability can corrupt the snapshot or misstate the pause.
applicability.refusal_point: Reject staging overlap that races checkpointed-state mutation; do not infer backend durability from asynchronous return or writer completion.

recommendations: Place the staging wait before the earliest mutation of any checkpointed state, including forward-mutated buffers rather than only optimizer.step.
Wait for the previous upload before reusing a stager's CPU storage; observe the final upload before closing caller-owned staging resources.
Measure checkpoint and intervening steps with the same state/cadence, retaining first-use and cached-buffer costs plus per-host memory and I/O pressure.
